question: Which of the following drug is contraindicated in a patient of myasthenia gravis: September 2008
analysis: Myasthenia gravis is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by muscle weakness and fatigue. Succinylcholine and Tubocurare are neuromuscular blocking agents that can exacerbate muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis. Pyridostigmine, on the other hand, is a cholinesterase inhibitor commonly used to treat myasthenia gravis by improving neuromuscular transmission. Halothane is a general anesthetic and is not contraindicated in myasthenia gravis.
